questions.question: The solution of dy/dx = 3x² is:
questions.rationale: Integrating both sides gives y = x³ + C — a family of curves; an initial condition would pin down C.

questions.question: The order of the equation d²y/dt² + y = 0 is:
questions.rationale: Order is the highest derivative present — here the second derivative, making it a second-order equation (of simple harmonic motion).

questions.question: Solve dy/dx = 2xy with y(0) = 3. Which is the particular solution?
questions.rationale: Separating: dy/y = 2x dx → ln|y| = x² + C → y = Ae^(x²); y(0) = 3 forces A = 3.

questions.question: The equation dy/dt = ky with k > 0 describes:
questions.rationale: The solution y = y₀e^(kt) grows without bound when k > 0; k < 0 gives decay.

questions.question: Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5,730 years. An artefact contains 25% of its original C-14. Its age is about:
questions.rationale: 25% survives after exactly two half-lives: 2 × 5,730 = 11,460 years.

questions.question: According to Newton's law of cooling, a hot object in a cooler room:
options: Cools fastest when hottest, approaching room temperature exponentially
Cools at a rate independent of temperature difference
questions.rationale: dT/dt = −k(T − Tₛ): the rate is proportional to the temperature excess, so cooling is fast at first and slows as T nears Tₛ.

questions.question: Money compounded continuously at 100% interest would grow according to:
questions.rationale: Continuous compounding follows dA/dt = rA with r = 1, giving A = A₀eᵗ — the birthplace of e.

questions.question: A separable differential equation is one where:
options: The variables can be split to opposite sides before integrating
questions.rationale: dy/dx = f(x)g(y) rearranges to dy/g(y) = f(x)dx, letting each side be integrated separately.

questions.question: The equation d²x/dt² = −ω²x describes simple harmonic motion. Its general solution is:
questions.rationale: Sinusoids have second derivative proportional to −x: x = A sin(ωt + φ) (equivalently a cosine mix) satisfies the equation.

questions.question: Unlike the exponential model, the logistic equation dP/dt = kP(1 − P/K) predicts:
options: Growth that flattens toward the carrying capacity K
questions.rationale: The (1 − P/K) factor brakes growth as P nears K, producing the S-curve seen in populations and technology adoption.
